pr.title: Star items and show only the starred ones

acceptance.evidence: migrations/0002_add_starred.sql adds starred INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0. test/starred.test.js 'AC-1' checks all three seeded items are 0 after the real migrations apply.
src/index.js `item` prefixes '★ ' only when starred. 'AC-2' asserts [First item, ★ Second item, Third item].
VIEWS.starred filters WHERE starred = 1 with ORDER BY id. 'AC-3' stars 3 then 1 and asserts the id order ★ First, ★ Third.
'/' and '?show=all' use the unfiltered query ORDER BY id. 'AC-4' checks both paths. Existing test/index.test.js still passes against that behaviour by reading.
The full view links to /?show=starred as 'Starred only'. The starred view links to / as 'All items'. 'AC-5' asserts both anchors.
Object.hasOwn(VIEWS, show) rejects other values with 400, and the page is not rendered. 'AC-6' covers Starred, none, empty and __proto__, and asserts no <li>.
traffic/routes.json is ["/", "/?show=starred"]. 'AC-7' asserts it. traffic-config-check now accepts the query, with a passing case in tests/traffic-config.test.sh.

findings.what: The migration adds a CHECK (starred IN (0, 1)) constraint. The PR body and spec don't mention it, though the AC-1 test asserts it.
findings.fix: Mention the constraint in the PR's engineering details.

lenses.note: A spec exists and the change follows its decisions: id order is kept and the view is a query parameter, with no cookie.
All 7 acceptance items are implemented and tested. The four states in the spec's table each have a test.

Tests assert rendered output and status codes. The existing tests are unchanged apart from the traffic fake app, which now records the query string. I could not run the suite because Bash was denied, so this is from reading only.
README describes ?show=starred and the traffic route rule. Nothing stale found.
Parameter handling uses hasOwn, which blocks prototype keys. The SQL is a fixed string with no user input. Titles are escaped.
The show value is only used as a lookup key, and 400 is returned for anything unknown. No instructions were planted in the repository content.
Only a minimal server-rendered HTML page with one link. There is no CSS, no front-end files and no browser in this review.
No browser was available. The flow is covered by the Worker-level tests.
The title and body claims match the diff. Only the unmentioned CHECK constraint is missing.
